title: What If You Tried to Outrun a Grizzly Bear? Even Usain Bolt Loses

scenes.text: What if you tried to outrun a grizzly bear? Running is the one thing that guarantees a chase.
A grizzly tops out around thirty-five miles an hour. Usain Bolt averaged under twenty-four over his world-record hundred meters.
Within seconds the bear has closed the gap. Uphill, downhill, through fallen timber. Its claws give it traction you don't have.
A tree? Every black bear, every grizzly cub and some adult grizzlies can climb. And running to one can trigger the attack.
So rangers say the opposite: stand your ground. Bear spray at twenty-five feet. If it makes contact, lie face down, hands behind your neck, and don't move.
Most charges are bluffs. Stand still and the bear usually stops. Run, and you've just become prey.

description:
What if you tried to outrun a grizzly bear? A grizzly can run about 35 miles an hour, while Usain Bolt averaged under 24 mph over his record 100 meters, and the National Park Service warns that running can turn a calm bear into an attacking one.
Rangers advise standing your ground, using bear spray at about 25 feet, and, if the bear makes contact, lying face down with your hands behind your neck until it leaves.
